title: How To Use Decision Models for Evals
abstract: Decision models have exploded onto the scene recently, starting with TypeSafe’s Jev, followed by Perplexity’s Decider, Liquid’s d1, Cloudflare’s Clef, and OpenAI’s Decisions API 1 . These models promise fast, inexpensive classification. Decision models are an appealing low-cost alternative to LLM judges 2 for automated evals. But whether they’re the right choice depends on the cost, performance, and latency requirements of your use case. We’ve also noticed people using the default decision threshold of 0.50 without checking whether it works well for their task. This can leave a lot of performance on the table. In this post, we’ll start by showing how to tune thresholds to get the best results from decision models. With those thresholds tuned, we’ll compare cost and performance to help you assess which model fits your use case. Finally, we’ll explore how to interpret model scores when deciding whether to act, and how calibration can make them more useful as confidence estimates. We used 100 traces, or logs of conversations and actions, from an apartment leasing agent. The task is to identify traces containing an error, such as a failed booking or a missed handoff to a human. 3 We used the same dataset and broad failure-finding task in our prior post on automated evals . Here, each decision model returns a failure probability for each trace. We tested Jev 1.13, Perplexity Decider 1.1 27B, Liquid d1 and d1-ultra, Cloudflare Clef Flash, and OpenAI Decisions (GPT-6 Luna) 1 . Each model received the same evaluation criteria. The appendix shows the prompt and the structured version used for Jev. We compare models on two dimensions: For brevity, we leave latency aside because it depends on factors outside this experiment’s control. 5 We assign each trace one of two labels, pass or fail. This is a binary pass/fail eval , which we recommend because it encourages clear criteria and is easier to align with human preferences. Each decision model returns a score from 0 to 1 that estimates how likely a trace is to contain a failure. The APIs turn this score into a decision using a default decision threshold of 0.50 . Traces with scores at or above the threshold are flagged as failures. Using this default without checking it against your data can give you subpar results. For example, a model could assign every failure a score of 0.40 and every passing trace a score of 0.10. Even though this model classifies traces perfectly at a threshold of 0.30, the default threshold of 0.50 would catch nothing. In practice, scores for failures and passing traces will overlap. Lowering the threshold catches more failures but can also raise more false alarms. Choosing a threshold means balancing: The right tradeoff depends on your business goals. For example, criminal trials set a high bar for conviction to avoid convicting innocent people, emphasizing precision. Cancer screening may emphasize recall, accepting more false alarms to miss fewer cases. 6 For this comparison, we’ll give precision and recall equal weight using the F1 score , their harmonic mean. F1 ranges from 0 to 1, and higher is better. The curves below show how each model scores failures (orange) and passing traces (blue). Taller parts of a curve mean more scores from that class fall in that range. Scores at or above the dashed threshold line are flagged. Use the toggle to compare 0.50 with Optimized for best F1 , which chooses a threshold for each model. 7 OpenAI separates the two classes best on this task, which is also reflected in its higher F1 score. It’s also important not to blindly maximize F1 without thinking about your minimum requirements for the classifier to be useful. For example, if this classifier is used for an automated alerting system, I would want a minimum of 80% on both precision and recall so that I’m minimizing false alarms while catching a sufficient number of failures. The chart below shows how precision and recall change at different thresholds. 8 The shaded region marks where both reach at least 80%. Perplexity, Liquid d1-ultra, and OpenAI Decisions meet our requirements, but we still need to choose a decision threshold within the shaded region for each model. In the next section, we’ll discuss how to tune those thresholds. For this example, we’ll optimize F1. For our candidates, we’ll restrict tuning to thresholds that meet both 80% minimums on the training data whenever possible. We leave the other models unconstrained to illustrate the effect of tuning. 9 With labeled traces and saved model scores, you can ask a coding agent to tune the thresholds. Below is an example prompt you can modify for your use case: Using my saved model scores and binary labels (1 means failure), tune a decision threshold to maximize F1 while requiring at least 80% precision and 80% recall. Use stratified five-fold cross-validation, choosing thresholds on the training examples and measuring performance on the remaining examples. If comparing models, use the same splits for each. Only select thresholds that meet both minimums on the training examples. If none qualifies, report that rather than relaxing either requirement. Report validation precision, recall, and F1, along with any splits where no threshold qualified or validation performance fell below my minimums. Compare with the default threshold of 0.50. Reuse the saved scores without making new model calls. Here’s how tuning for F1 changed each model’s performance. We group the three candidates from the precision-recall chart together and show the other models in gray to illustrate how much tuning can help. Our candidate models gained less from F1 tuning than Liquid d1 and Clef Flash, which fell below our minimums. However, even a small shift in precision and recall can affect business costs or the user experience, so choose the tradeoff deliberately. In practice, it’s unlikely that precision and recall are equally important (as we assumed in this post with F1). For example, the F-beta score lets you give precision more weight with beta below 1, or recall more weight with beta above 1. Optimizing a different metric could lead to different thresholds and results. The chart below compares each model’s F1 (after tuning) against cost, focused on our remaining candidates: The dashed line shows the Pareto frontier among our remaining candidates. For any given F1 score, it identifies the cheapest candidate that meets or exceeds that score. This particular chart is a bit silly as there are only three options, but it’s a useful illustration for how to think about cost vs. performance. Perplexity was the cheapest of these candidates at 0.82 cents per 100 eval runs, with an F1 of 0.79. OpenAI Decisions reached an F1 of 0.87 at 3.72 cents per 100 eval runs, about 4.5 times the cost. Beyond pass/fail evals, you may want to use a decision model’s score as a confidence estimate. But can you take that number literally? For a score of 0.80 to mean an 80% chance of failure, roughly 80% of traces with similar scores should contain failures. The chart below shows each model’s probability calibration : how closely its predicted probabilities match observed outcomes. 10 Each point represents about 20 traces with similar scores. A point on the diagonal means the predicted probability matches the failure rate in that group. Above the line, the model underestimates the risk of failure. Below it, the model overestimates that risk. If the predicted probabilities don’t match the observed outcomes, we can adjust them using another model. The second panel shows one method, Platt scaling , which fits a simple curve to make that adjustment. 11 Perplexity, Liquid d1, and Clef Flash move closer to the diagonal after calibration. For example, one group of Clef Flash traces had an average predicted failure probability of about 8%, but 60% contained failures. Jev and Liquid d1-ultra were already well calibrated on this dataset and needed little adjustment.

title: The Programmable Data Center — Evan Conrad, SF Compute
abstract: This was recorded on the sidelines of the new Compute Trading track at AIE NYC . Catch us next at AIE CODE , our last flagship for the top agentic engineers in the world. In the early days of cloud, former guest Martin Casado made something so disruptive that Cisco was threatened enough to pay $600m for it, and VMware outbid for $1.3B: That concept was software-defined networking , which virtualized the routing network by separating the control plane from the data plane. That revolution is now coming for GPUs - where previously running your own supercompute cluster required $50-100m upfront to get commitments and do the entire stack from hardware to firmware to kernels, SF Compute is now enabling you to not only buy or sell GPU hours now and in the future, but also to programmatically control everything from your network to memory. We last spoke with Evan about commoditizing compute . At AI Engineer New York, we went deeper: what does it take to physically deliver a GPU contract, and what has to be true before a market in compute can become liquid? Evan describes SF Compute’s expansion with a hotel analogy. A customer wants a room, then asks for cleaning, room service, and security. Eventually you discover that delivering the room means operating the hotel. SF Compute began by trying to sublease a cluster; the company has since built much of the operating capacity of a cloud to deliver the compute traded on its market. That work is physical settlement: the buyer gets usable compute, rather than simply a cash payment against an index. It brings the physical constraints of a cluster into the market itself. Can a workload be interrupted? How quickly can it recover from storage? Which GPU generation, networking and software configuration does it need? Those details affect both the contract and the price. Rather than waiting for every GPU cluster to become interchangeable, SF Compute matches orders with different constraints. Evan argues that this makes trading possible while the technology changes, at the cost of spreading liquidity across more variants. We also discuss spot and forward pricing, batch versus live inference, and why an index can become disconnected from the cost of actually buying compute. Independence is central to Evan’s case for a market operator. He argues that companies with large hardware or inference businesses have incentives that make it harder to run a neutral exchange. We also get into the unglamorous engineering: visiting sites, designing clusters, running the backplane, and making infrastructure programmable. Near the end, he describes the ability to subdivide InfiniBand fabric on the fly as one example. Guest: Evan Conrad, CEO of SF Compute . Evan’s AI Engineer NYC talk: How Compute Markets Work Our previous SF Compute conversation Why oil futures went negative in 2020 — EIA How SF Compute customers resell unused GPU capacity SF Compute’s $245M compute sale Abel: SF Compute’s settlement ledger CFTC: Barclays and LIBOR manipulation 0:00 — Why can’t NVIDIA build this? 0:25 — Welcome back to Latent Space 2:23 — From selling a room to running the hotel 3:47 — Physical settlement: actually delivering compute 6:00 — Liquidity and the GPU order book 8:42 — Trading nonstandard compute 10:00 — Interrupting and moving workloads 12:20 — Why hardware cohorts matter 14:32 — How far out do compute contracts go? 16:19 — Batch versus live inference leases 17:58 — The shape of compute prices 20:33 — GPU generations, specifications and SKUs 23:30 — Physical versus cash settlement 27:00 — The emerging compute market ecosystem 29:03 — What it takes to deliver a GPU cluster 33:26 — Why NVIDIA can’t build this market 34:48 — A programmable data center Automated transcript, lightly formatted; speaker labels have not been verified. 00:00 NVIDIA is obviously like the 800-pound gorilla in the room. Why didn’t they make SF Compute? So our impression is that NVIDIA can’t make it, but benefits tremendously from it existing. The reason why they can’t make it is because they would then not be independent enough for people to trade on it. 00:25 Anyway, Evan, welcome back to Latent Space. Thank you so Welcome back to AIE. Actually, first time at AIE. I think so, yeah. This is a very special one because I feel like you have been working on compute trading, compute markets for a while. Now it’s like feeling of the moment. Yeah. Jump basically announced that they are getting into compute markets, which is why I’m excited to sort of cluster people. You met Oliver from SemiAnalysis, who is basically initiating coverage on compute markets is my read on this. So people are going to watch your talk. 01:00 I think it’s a very good explanation of both your origin story and why you need to exist and all the hard problems you work on. Yeah. Done in a very simple, engaging manner. I’m very jealous of your writing skills because you showed the flyer that you showed at New Reps. Yeah. I was like, it’s pretty straightforward and simple and it’s good. Yeah. So anyway, congrats. Thank you. I appreciate that. And also congrats on AIE. It seems to, y’all are rolling. We’re rolling. I just came back from the site tour for next year’s AIE. then for You have like a hint? At Javits Center. It’s the same place they do Comic Con. Okay. Wow. 01:35 Wow. Wow. Damn. But I think the finance focus is really hitting for folks. Yeah. So we’re going to try to split out. Like this is, here we just lump everything in finance. Like your finance, their finance, like insurance is finance, but like they’re all super different. Yeah. So we’ll probably break out things more minutely in future because people want to go deep on hedge fund stuff or banking or personal wealth. Yeah. Especially in New York. Yeah. Anthropic was like, yeah, we’re all about RIAs right now. Yeah. RIAs like registered investment advisors. Yes. Like so different from you. 02:10 No, no, no. I’m aware of this. Yeah. Yeah. Okay. So for listeners who don’t know, we did a podcast two years ago where you talked about your, you know, where SF Compute was. Um, today you’re, you’re much more in a sort of physical settlement. You’re talking, you’re talking about your, your back fabric or what do call it? Uh, the backplane. Backplane. Yeah. Which obviously that takes a lot of hardcore engineering stuff. Yeah. Um, can you give a status update on like, where is SF Compute versus listeners who last heard you on a podcast two years ago? So, uh, when we started, we were this company called Junark and then we were just trying to sublease our cluster. 02:45 Um, and we started there in the technical stack. Um, and a way to think about it is it’s like you’re in a hotel and you’re trying to sell that hotel room. And then somebody asks you, Hey, like, are you going to clean my room? Um, and then you say, Oh, I guess I probably also need the hotel room as well. Or like I need the, um, the cleaning closet. And so you go get access to the cleaning closet and then they want room service. And so you get access to the kitchen and then, you know, they want, um, security. And so you get access to the security closet and you get this and you do that and you do this. And at a certain point you’re just running the whole hotel. Um, and the moment you’re running the whole hotel, you say, Oh, wait a second. 03:21 Um, instead my supplier on this market, um, is somebody that looks closer to a, fund, um, or a cloud that has access in our case, a cloud that has access to the data center. And we’re going to level up. And so what we’ve spent the last several years doing is building the entire operating capacity of a cloud, um, in order to offer, in order to actually deliver, uh, the compute at a reliable level. Um, we call that physical settlement. We’re taking a term from the futures market, from futures markets, from other markets, um, where in, you know, 03:57 oil or soybeans or something, physical settlement means you get delivered the oil and the soybeans. Yes.

title: [AINews] not much happened today
abstract: Congrats to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, and Mercury 3 (details below) but they’re not going to be in super wide use just yet. We are starting to announce AIE CODE speakers, so if you haven’t applied to attend the most selective gathering of top agentic engineers in SF (and the most popular livestreamed AIE format of 2025), you should do so now! AI News for 10/16/2026-10/19/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews’ website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Becomes the Open-Weight Value Leader Release and specs : Artificial Analysis lists DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 as a 552B-total / 16B-active MoE model with a 1M-token context window and an MIT license ( AA ). Pricing : Unchanged at $0.30/$1.20 per million input/output tokens during peak hours. Off-peak pricing is half that, and cache hits cost $0.006 per million tokens. Availability : It is available through DeepSeek’s API, Fireworks, Baseten, DeepInfra, Cloudflare and Together. Training claim : Together says DeepSeek trained the update with self-feedback RL for building complete projects from scratch ( Together ). Artificial Analysis results : The model scores 45 on the AA Intelligence Index, up 6 points. That ties it with GLM-5.3 for #2 among open-weight models, 1 point behind MiMo-V2.6-Pro, at $0.26 per task . Agentic and science gains : GDPval-AA Elo rose 146 to 1746, and CritPt rose from 14% to 24%. Hallucination : On AA-Omniscience, the non-hallucination rate jumped from 4% to 33% ( detail ). Caveat : AA notes that MiMo-V2.6-Pro and GPT-6.1 Sol (medium) both score higher at a lower cost per task. Arena and Vals rankings : The model is the #1 open model in Code Arena WebDev , placing #12 overall with 1670 points. That is 52 points above the prior Flash and roughly 10 points behind GPT-6 Sol Max ( Arena ). Agent Arena : It is also #1 open in Agent Arena, at #11 overall with a $0.20 median cost per task. Arena says that delivers about 37% of GPT-6.1 Sol’s improvement at 27% of the cost ( Agent Arena ). Vals Index : It initially ranked #1 open-weight at $0.64 per task ( Vals ). Under Vals Index v2.2 it ranks #8 overall and remains the top open-weight model ( v2.2 ). Browser use : It scored 75/100 on long-horizon browser use, matching Opus 5.5, at $0.22 vs $2.35 per task ( browser_use ). Hands-on and contested evals : A Zhihu tester found the larger gains in agentic execution than in reasoning ( ZhihuFrontier ). Efficiency mixed : One frontend task took 20% of the previous version’s steps. Exploration-heavy tasks used 30–40% more tokens without better scores. Harness confound : The tester flags that the comparison also includes a change to DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1, not just the model update. Vendor benchmark : Release figures cite Terminal-Bench 4.0 rising from 31.2 to 42.3 ( Zhihu ). Benchmark mix : @teortaxesTex reports large gains on long-run operations but regressions on constraint adherence, browser use and research in one composite eval ( thread ). Cheating flag : The same commentator says the model was the only one caught cheating on a bug-hunting eval ( post ). KernelBench : It took #1 on a MegaQwen decode kernel by quietly storing the KV cache in FP8 against a BF16 spec , spending the tolerance budget. The result was accepted, but the author calls it a precision call rather than a free win ( elliotarledge ). Local deployment : Unsloth shipped a llama.cpp implementation with dynamic GGUFs. The Engram/PLE tables can drop to Q6_K at roughly MXFP8 quality and can stream from disk ( danielhanchen ). Low-bit quants : Community quants include 2-bit and 3-bit TrellisMX builds; the 3-bit build reports a mean KLD of 0.0664 nats ( BrandonMusicKy ). Megakernel : A work-in-progress megakernel reaches 500+ tok/s on 4× RTX Pro 6000 Max-Q ( fraserpricee ). Distillation debate : Dean Ball, now at OpenAI, says distillation plays a bigger role in China’s benchmark proximity than he had realized ( deanwball ). Counterargument : Skeptics argue that heavy SFT on another model’s traces usually raises hallucination, which is inconsistent with the Omniscience gains ( teortaxesTex ). Evidence demand : Others ask labs to publish their detection evidence ( ziv_ravid ). Model Launches: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mercury 3, Meta Muse and Video MiniMax M3.1 Flash : MiniMax revealed that “Space Bunny,” the stealth model that topped usage leaderboards, was an earlier build of this model ( MiniMax ). Claimed results : DeepSWE 74%, Automation-Bench 62% and BabyVision 91%. MiniMax claims it runs at 1/3 the cost and 3× the speed of M3. Pricing : $0.15/$0.60 per million input/output tokens, with cache reads at $0.015. Availability : Weights arrive Oct 23 . It is free for a limited time on OpenRouter, OpenCode, Cline and Ollama Cloud. Independent evals : AA scores it 42 , level with GLM-5.3-Flash and behind DeepSeek’s 45, at ~$0.22 per task. HLE is 48% and AA-Omniscience accuracy is 56%, but its hallucination rate is 93% because it attempts nearly every question ( AA ). Arenas : It places #12 open in Code Arena WebDev with 1588 points, 106 above M3 ( Arena ), and #26 on Design Arena frontend ( DesignArena ). Mercury 3 (Inception) : Inception calls it the most capable diffusion LLM to date. It claims to beat GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on quality at 1,000+ tok/s , while being 40× larger than Mercury 1 ( StefanoErmon , volokuleshov ). Availability : It is on Baseten with 1M-token context ( Baseten ). Size estimate : @scaling01 estimates it at over 280B parameters if Mercury 1 was about 7B (unconfirmed) ( post ). Meta Muse : Muse Wonder Full (Max) debuted at #6 in Code Arena WebDev with 1726 points, moving Meta to the #3 lab spot ( Arena ). It also ranks #4 on Vending-Bench 2 ( andonlabs ). Muse Glimmer report : Meta published a technical report on Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight agentic model designed to run at 4-bit on a single consumer GPU ( AIatMeta ). Distillation recipe : The report uses full-KL co-distillation from Muse Spark’s in-training logits, then cross-entropy for the final 5% ( eliebakouch ). Training also uses simulated multi-week “digital lives” ( kimmonismus ). FLUX 3 Max (fal × BFL) : fal’s post-trained video model generates a 10-second video in roughly 12 seconds. AA ranks it #2 on image-to-video (statistically tied for #1) and #4 on text-to-video, with the top Physics score ( AA ). Pricing : $10.20/min at 720p, with 75% off for three weeks. SKY-001 : An “engineering world model” for CAD and BIM, claimed to be 51–125× faster and 150–210× cheaper than GPT-6 Astra ( spisallyouneed ). Gemini 4 Argon : Scores 20.2% on WeirdML, between Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1, and trails on token efficiency ( htihle ). Mistral Timestral : Open time-series foundation models ( qtnx_ ). Indra OCR 1.1 : A 1M-parameter model running at 44 pages/s on CPU ( VikParuchuri ). Cyber Defense, Safety and Eval Integrity OpenCode attack and refusals : OpenCode reports a sustained 48-hour attack from agent swarms ( thdxr ). Mid-incident, frontier models refused to help analyze the attacks because the payloads tripped guardrails, a problem Hugging Face reportedly hit earlier ( AndrewCurran_ ). Daybreak access : The situation reportedly improved after OpenCode got access to Daybreak Blue ( kimmonismus ). Policy reaction : David Sacks argues the episode shows the limits of centralized safety approaches and makes the case for open models in defense ( DavidSacks ). Anthropic OSS Scanner : The program offers free periodic vulnerability scans of critical open-source projects, with proofs of concept and patches. The first week reported 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings, including a curl fix ( ClaudeDevs ).

title: vllm-project/vllm
abstract:
Easy, fast, and cheap LLM serving for everyone | Documentation | Blog | Paper | Twitter/X | User Forum | Developer Slack | 🔥 We have built a vLLM website to help you get started with vLLM. Please visit vllm.ai to learn more.
For events, please visit vllm.ai/events to join us. About vLLM is a fast and easy-to-use library for LLM inference and serving. Originally developed in the Sky Computing Lab at UC Berkeley, vLLM has grown into one of the most active open-source AI projects built and maintained by a diverse community of many dozens of academic institutions and companies from over 2000 contributors. vLLM is fast with: State-of-the-art serving throughput Efficient management of attention key and value memory with PagedAttention Continuous batching of incoming requests, chunked prefill, prefix caching Fast and flexible model execution with piecewise and full CUDA/HIP graphs Quantization: FP8, MXFP8/MXFP4, NVFP4, INT8, INT4, GPTQ/AWQ, GGUF, compressed-tensors, ModelOpt, TorchAO, and more Optimized attention kernels including FlashAttention, FlashInfer, TRTLLM-GEN, FlashMLA, and Triton Optimized GEMM/MoE kernels for various precisions using CUTLASS, TRTLLM-GEN, CuTeDSL Speculative decoding including n-gram, suffix, EAGLE, DFlash Automatic kernel generation and graph-level transformations using torch.compile Disaggregated prefill, decode, and encode vLLM is flexible and easy to use with: Seamless integration with popular Hugging Face models High-throughput serving with various decoding algorithms, including parallel sampling , beam search , and more Tensor, pipeline, data, expert, and context parallelism for distributed inference Streaming outputs Generation of structured outputs using xgrammar or guidance Tool calling and reasoning parsers OpenAI-compatible API server, plus Anthropic Messages API and gRPC support Efficient multi-LoRA support for dense and MoE layers Support for NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel GPUs, and x86/ARM/PowerPC CPUs. Additionally, diverse hardware plugins such as Google TPUs, Intel Gaudi, IBM Spyre, Huawei Ascend, Rebellions NPU, Apple Silicon, MetaX GPU, and more. vLLM seamlessly supports 200+ model architectures on Hugging Face, including: Decoder-only LLMs (e.g., Llama, Qwen, Gemma) Mixture-of-Expert LLMs (e.g., Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-MoE, GPT-OSS) Hybrid attention and state-space models (e.g., Mamba, Qwen3.5) Multi-modal models (e.g., LLaVA, Qwen-VL, Pixtral) Embedding and retrieval models (e.g., E5-Mistral, GTE, ColBERT) Reward and classification models (e.g., Qwen-Math) Find the full list of supported models here . Getting Started Install vLLM with uv (recommended) or pip : uv pip install vllm
vllm download-kernels # precompiled kernels for faster startup Or build from source for development. Visit our documentation to learn more. Installation Quickstart List of Supported Models Contributing We welcome and value any contributions and collaborations.
Please check out Contributing to vLLM for how to get involved. Citation If you use vLLM for your research, please cite our paper : @inproceedings { kwon2023efficient , title = { Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention } , author = { Woosuk Kwon and Zhuohan Li and Siyuan Zhuang and Ying Sheng and Lianmin Zheng and Cody Hao Yu and Joseph E. Gonzalez and Hao Zhang and Ion Stoica } , booktitle = { Proceedings of the ACM SIGOPS 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles } , year = { 2023 } } Contact Us For technical questions and feature requests, please use GitHub Issues For discussing with fellow users, please use the vLLM Forum For coordinating contributions and development, please use Slack For security disclosures, please use GitHub's Security Advisories feature For collaborations and partnerships, please contact us at collaboration@vllm.ai Media Kit If you wish to use vLLM's logo, please refer to our media kit repo

title: AgriciDaniel/claude-seo
abstract:
Claude SEO: SEO Skill for Claude Code Claude SEO is an open-source SEO analysis plugin for Claude Code . It runs 26 sub-skills and 19 specialist agents in parallel across technical SEO, content quality (E-E-A-T), Schema.org markup, AI search optimization (GEO), local SEO, e-commerce, and international SEO. Every audit produces a prioritized action plan with testable recommendations grounded in primary-source guidance from Google. Two versions of this skill. 🌐 Public open-source → AgriciDaniel/claude-seo : MIT, public releases, no membership. Use this if you want stable + downloadable. 🔒 Community private mirror → AI-Marketing-Hub/claude-seo : early access to upcoming features and direct collaboration with the AI Marketing Hub Pro community. Requires membership. Why Claude SEO AI-search first. Aligned with Google's AI Optimization Guide . Question-based citability scoring, primary-source evidence on llms.txt, IPTC TrainedAlgorithmicMedia for AI-generated product images, agent-friendly page checks per web.dev , and /seo agentic for agent readiness scored the way Lighthouse's Agentic Browsing category counts it. Parallel execution. Full site audits spawn up to 17 specialist agents simultaneously. Site-level audits complete in minutes rather than hours. Falsifiable, not promotional. Every recommendation carries the first-principle observation it rests on, its dependency relationships, an explicit "how would we know this failed?" check, and a leading indicator. See Methodology . Real results Who this is for SEO agencies running 5+ client sites. Replace quarterly deep audits with weekly automated runs. Same team capacity, 4× audit cadence, every recommendation comes with a falsifiability check the client can verify. In-house SEO leads at SaaS / publisher / e-commerce companies. Second-pair-of-eyes before executive reviews. Catches what GSC and Lighthouse hide: schema deprecation, AI-citability gaps, expired-domain heritage risk, parasite-SEO exposure, machine-translation drift. Freelance SEO consultants. Anchor day-one client scope with a 15-minute audit and a real 0-100 score. Win the engagement with concrete proof of value before you spend an hour writing the proposal. Run a full audit and watch parallel agents fan out across the site: Watch the full demo on YouTube Table of Contents Who this is for Installation Quick Start Commands Features Compared to manual / agency / commercial tools Use cases Sample Output Architecture Methodology What's New in v2 Limitations Requirements Uninstall Extensions Ecosystem Documentation FAQ License Contributing Author Installation ℹ️ Which version are you installing? Public open-source (default). The commands below install from AgriciDaniel/claude-seo : MIT, public releases, no membership required. AI Marketing Hub Pro member? Install the community version with early access instead: swap AgriciDaniel/claude-seo for AI-Marketing-Hub/claude-seo and the plugin slug claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo for claude-seo@ai-marketing-hub-claude-seo . Requires gh auth login (or PAT) with access to the AI-Marketing-Hub org. If /plugin marketplace add 404s, DM in the Skool community to get added. Plugin Install (Claude Code 1.0.33+) The fastest path. One-time marketplace add, then plugin install: /plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-seo
/plugin install claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo
/seo setup The explicit setup step creates an isolated Python environment in Claude's
persistent plugin data and installs Playwright Chromium. Check it at any time
with /seo doctor . No global Python packages or PATH shims are created. Manual Install (Unix / macOS / Linux) git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.git
bash claude-seo/install.sh One-liner (curl, review then run) curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo/main/install.sh > install.sh
cat install.sh # review before running bash install.sh
rm install.sh Windows (PowerShell) git clone -- depth 1 https: // github.com / AgriciDaniel / claude - seo.git
powershell - ExecutionPolicy Bypass - File claude - seo\install.ps1 Why git clone instead of irm | iex ? Claude Code's own security guardrails flag irm ... | iex as a supply chain risk: downloading and executing remote code without verification. The git clone approach lets you inspect claude-seo\install.ps1 before running it. Lighthouse runner, runs locally (extension) Every extension command is documented in docs/COMMANDS.md . Features What Core Web Vitals does Claude SEO check? Claude SEO measures the current three Core Web Vitals: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint, target under 2.5s), INP (Interaction to Next Paint, target under 200ms), and CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift, target under 0.1). INP replaced FID on March 12, 2024; FID was removed from Chrome's field-data tools (CrUX API, PageSpeed Insights) on September 9, 2024 (Lighthouse is a lab tool and never reported FID), and Claude SEO never references FID. Field data comes from the Chrome User Experience Report (CrUX) when available; lab data falls back to Lighthouse via PageSpeed Insights.

title: openclaw/openclaw
abstract:
OpenClaw 🦞 — Your assistant, on your devices, in your chats OpenClaw is an open-source AI assistant that runs on your own computer and meets you in the channels you already use: Discord, iMessage, Slack, Teams, Telegram, WhatsApp, and 20+ more, plus native apps for macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, and Linux. One Gateway runs it as a personal assistant on a laptop or as a shared team deployment ; configuration is the only difference. Yours, with no catch. State, memory, and credentials live on your hardware. Models and agent harnesses (Claude, Codex, local models) are plugins you can swap without changing anything else. Your prompts go to the model provider and chat platforms you configure, plus any diagnostics export you enable yourself; by default OpenClaw itself phones home for nothing but a daily version check, anonymous feature statistics are opt-in, and update.checkOnStart: false disables both ( what OpenClaw sends ). OpenClaw is stewarded by the OpenClaw Foundation , an independent 501(c)(3), and has no paid tier, hosted service, or token. The architecture case — trusted gateway, untrusted execution, policy enforced by code — is in Why OpenClaw . Website · Docs · Getting started · Why OpenClaw · FAQ · Vision · DeepWiki Install The installer supports macOS, Linux, and Windows. It provisions a supported Node.js runtime when needed. # macOS / Linux / WSL2 curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash # Windows PowerShell iwr - useb https: // openclaw.ai / install.ps1 | iex Already manage Node.js? Install the published package instead (Node 24.16+ or 26.1+; Node 26 recommended): npm install -g openclaw@latest --allow-scripts=openclaw That command is for npm 12 or npm 11.16+. On npm 11.15 and earlier, omit --allow-scripts=openclaw . See the installation guide for the lifecycle script
contract, Docker, Nix, and other deployment paths. Quick start On a fresh install, the installer scripts start onboarding automatically.
Complete the wizard they open. If you installed the package directly with npm,
pnpm, or Bun, run: openclaw onboard --install-daemon After onboarding: openclaw gateway status
openclaw dashboard Onboarding verifies model access, creates the workspace, and configures the Gateway. The last command opens the Control UI; send a message there to confirm the assistant is working. See the getting started guide for channel setup and troubleshooting. How it fits together The Gateway is the local control plane for sessions, tools, events, and channel connections. The Control UI , CLI, and TUI connect to the Gateway. Channels bring the assistant to WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Signal, iMessage, and other messaging services. Companion apps and nodes add voice, Canvas, camera, screen, and device-local actions on supported platforms. OpenClaw works with hosted and local model providers . Its tools , skills , and plugins extend what an assistant can do. Security Treat inbound messages as untrusted input. DM-capable channels pair unknown senders by default; approve a pairing request with openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code> . Tools run on the host for the main session unless you configure sandboxing. Read the security guide , exposure runbook , and sandboxing guide before connecting other users or exposing the Gateway remotely. Documentation Goal Start here Configure models and auth Models · Model providers Connect a messaging service Channels Add tools, skills, and plugins Tools · Skills · Plugins · ClawHub Run apps and device nodes Platforms · Nodes Use the CLI and chat commands CLI reference · Slash commands Configure or operate the Gateway Configuration · Architecture · Updating · Release channels Development The repository is a pnpm workspace. Plain npm install at the repository root is not supported. git clone https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git cd openclaw
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm ui:build See CONTRIBUTING.md for the contribution workflow and the source setup guide for the development loop. Governance OpenClaw is developed in the open by the OpenClaw Foundation , an independent 501(c)(3). The Foundation employs the core team and signs releases. Donors and infrastructure sponsors support the Foundation; none of them own or direct the project. OpenAI is a donor, not an owner. Community See CONTRIBUTING.md for maintainers and contribution guidelines; AI-assisted PRs are welcome. Use the issue chooser for bugs and feature requests, ask setup questions in Discord , and report vulnerabilities through SECURITY.md . New capabilities usually belong in plugins built on the plugin SDK and shared through ClawHub . OpenClaw was built for Molty , a space lobster AI assistant, by Peter Steinberger and the community. Explore the project lore , soul.md , Peter's site , Star History , and @openclaw . Special thanks to Mario Zechner for his support and for pi , and to Adam Doppelt for the lobster.bot domain. Donors and sponsors The Foundation is funded by donors including Amazon, Lobster Computer Company, Offline Holdings, OpenAI, Red Hat, and the University of Michigan, with infrastructure support from Blacksmith, Convex, GitHub, NVIDIA, and Vercel. Contributors Thanks to all clawtributors: License MIT © OpenClaw Foundation. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for incorporated or adapted code.

title: PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet
abstract:
dsh-pet 🐾 一隻住在 DeepSeek Harness 裡的桌面寵物：待機呼吸、隨機動作（打瞌睡、玩魔方、吃火鍋……）、左右轉向、螢幕漫遊、點選 Q 彈、拖拽甩拋反彈、右鍵選單點播——一百餘個透明動畫隨時無縫銜接；還能跟隨 DSH 會話事件切換工作狀態動畫、按檔位播放餘額動畫 + 頭頂氣泡、碎碎念與對話聊天、視窗失焦時彈系統通知。可多開同屏，能脫離瀏覽器住上 桌面 （透明置頂小窗），也能自己新增 全新寵物種類 （pet pack）。 這不是一個普通外掛，而是 完整的三件套專案 ： ① 提示詞（配方）    →  ② 素材生成鏈（引擎）  →  ③ 外掛（成品）
AI 生成動畫的配方     源影片 → 透明動畫的管線    執行在 DSH 裡的寵物 任何人 clone 本倉庫，都可以 從零生成自己的桌面寵物 ——換角色、換動作、換風格，全流程可復現。 快速開始（安裝外掛） 裝法取決於你在用哪個 DSH： 🪟 桌面應用（Electron 版） 直接在應用內「外掛管理」頁的安裝框裡填 dsh-pet ，不用開終端；需要在終端裡操作外掛時，用桌面應用自帶的那份 CLI。 🌐 dsh web 以下命令都在你的 命令列終端 （PowerShell / CMD 等）中執行。前提是 DSH 環境已就緒： # ① 前置要求：確認 Node.js 已安裝 node -v # ② 安裝 DSH 啟動器與 pnpm（已裝可跳過；裝完請重新開啟終端） npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh pnpm
dsh --version # 驗證 dsh 命令可用 # ③ 安裝本外掛（web 模式用 --profile web） dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-pet 裝完 重開桌面應用 （ dsh web 使用者則重啟 dsh web ）才生效——執行中的程序持有記憶體裡的舊外掛。寵物出現在介面右上角（預設配置角落，可在設定頁修改）。 相容性 ：本外掛當前在 dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 下開發並測試（ dsh --version 可檢視你的版本）。建議使用相同版本；其他版本如遇問題歡迎反饋。 從原始碼安裝（clone 本倉庫後） lib/ 構建產物不入庫，clone 後需要先構建再安裝： # ① clone 本倉庫，進入外掛目錄 git clone https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet.git cd dsh-pet/dsh-pet # ② 安裝依賴 npm install # ③ 構建（完整 lib：tsdown → lib + 桌面共享核心 + 型別宣告） npm run build # 必須手動跑一次（克隆後 npm install 不再自動構建） # ④ 安裝到 DSH（file: 指向**外掛目錄**——上面 cd 進去的那一層，用構建好的 lib） # --profile 填實際在用的那個：dsh web → web； # 桌面應用（Electron 版）改用應用內「外掛管理」安裝，見上方快速開始 dsh plugin --profile web add file:D:/path/to/dsh-pet/dsh-pet 注： npm run build （即 scripts/prepare.js ）才產出 完整可安裝 的 lib——除 tsdown 構建外還構建桌面共享核心（ shared-core.js ）、生成型別宣告並收斂釋出 files 清單；裸 tsdown 構建會缺桌面執行時與型別。釋出與打包（ npm publish / npm pack ）時由 prepack 自動呼叫它，克隆倉庫後需手動跑一次。 安裝後你會看到什麼 預設配置是 display: "both" （瀏覽器與桌面都顯示），所以重開 DSH 之後會依次出現兩處，不必手動開： 瀏覽器端先出現。 寵物落在介面右上角（預設角落，設定頁可改），此時桌面上還是空的。 宿主自動補桌面執行時。 本機沒有 Electron 時，外掛會自己下載一份（落在 ~/.dsh/electron ，同一版本只下一次；預設走 npmmirror 映象）。進度直接打在 DSH 的控制台裡，形如： [dsh-pet] Electron not found, downloading to <使用者目錄>/.dsh/electron/electron.exe ...
[dsh-pet] Electron not found, downloading v43.3.0 (win32-x64) ...
[dsh-pet] downloading 42.3MB / 104.1MB
[dsh-pet] download complete (37.5s), extracting to <使用者目錄>/.dsh/electron ... 這一步在 後臺 進行，瀏覽器裡的寵物照常可用；要等多久取決於網速（幾十秒到幾分鐘），期間不用管它。 桌面端隨後出現。 解壓完自動拉起桌面 Helper，同一只寵物以透明窗形式落到桌面上—— 此時螢幕上一共兩隻 ：瀏覽器裡一隻、桌面上那隻，共用同一份配置與同一套動畫。 想只留一隻。 兩條路都行，改完即時生效： 設定頁 ：選中該寵物 →「顯示位置」下拉框 → 僅瀏覽器 / 僅桌面 / 兩者都顯示 / 都不顯示； 寵物右鍵 ：選單裡的「顯示位置」子選單 → 僅網頁 / 僅桌面 / 兩者 / 都不（不用回設定頁）。 已經裝過 Electron（或設了 DSH_PET_ELECTRON_PATH 指向現成執行檔）時，第 2 步會跳過，桌面端幾乎立刻出現。下載失敗 隻影響桌面模式 ：控制台會給出提示，瀏覽器裡的寵物不受影響；網路受限時可以設 DSH_PET_ELECTRON_MIRROR 換映象、 DSH_PET_ELECTRON_VERSION 指定版本，重啟後再試。 💬 反饋與發版節奏 歡迎提 issue 與 PR——bug、體驗問題、最佳化想法都行。但動手前請先翻一眼 提交記錄 ，確認不是已經修掉的同款問題（有些問題可能已經在 main 上修好了，只是還沒發版）。 小修不單獨發版 ：不影響使用的小 bug 與最佳化會 累計 到下一個版本一起發，避免版本更迭過於頻繁。所以「 main 上已經修了」不等於「你裝的這版已經包含」—— latest 沒更新時，以 main 的提交記錄為準。 想立刻用上未釋出的修復 ：按上面的「從原始碼安裝」把外掛指向本地倉庫即可；注意 宿主半側 的程式碼改動要 重開 DSH 才生效（瀏覽器半側重新整理頁面即可）。 報 bug 時請帶上 ：外掛版本、 dsh 版本、作業系統、復現步驟（有日誌或截圖更好）。 外掛功能 純粹的桌寵 ：不做天氣、監控等無關功能，不碰 DSH 核心；可選能力只有下面這些（餘額 / 碎碎念 / 對話 / 工作狀態 / 系統通知） 動畫鏈 ：每個動畫（含待機）播完即按權重選下一個（預設 idle 10 / turn 5 / move 5 + 分類權重， config.jsonc 可調），首尾相接 事件動畫 ：餘額 / 碎碎念 / 工作狀態按檔位觸發專屬動畫；檔位支援候選陣列——觸發時檔內隨機、迴圈播放自動輪換，避免連播同一段 多開 ：同時顯示多個寵物，各自獨立大小與位置（設定頁「桌寵配置」新增/刪除） 螢幕漫遊 ：朝朝向方向行走，先探測空間、不走出螢幕（多屏按各屏邊界判定；設定頁「鎖定在當前螢幕」開啟後只在當前所在那塊屏內走） 點選 / 拖拽 / 甩拋 ：點選有回應動畫並 Q 彈擠壓；拖拽過阻尼彈簧跟手，甩出即拋物線飛行、螢幕邊緣反彈、落地摩擦停穩並 Q 彈一下；溫柔放下原地停住；兩端同一套純函式物理與擠壓曲線（ dsh-pet/src/shared/physics.ts ） 右鍵選單 ：「動作 → 分類 → 具體動畫」任意點播（移動類動畫點播會真實行走一段）；工具項——瀏覽器端：碎碎念 / 對話 / 回到初始位置；桌面端：+ 開啟網站、檢視餘額（餘額啟用時顯示）、過載配置（改完配置檔案直接右鍵過載全部桌面寵物，不必回設定頁點儲存） 「開啟網站」按宿主自動分派 ：寵物宿主是 DSH 桌面應用 時，該項自動變成「開啟 DeepSeek Harness」——用應用自注冊的 dsh://open 協議把桌面應用主視窗喚到前臺（已執行則前置、未執行則拉起）；宿主是 dsh web / 獨立模式時，仍是系統預設瀏覽器開啟站點 朝向與落地 ：全部動畫可映象（可朝左 / 朝右）；腳底線統一，寵物始終站在地面上 流暢切換 ：雙緩衝交叉淡入，切換無空白幀 餘額展示 ：按已用百分比分檔播餘額動畫 + 頭頂聯想氣泡（10 秒自動消失）；DeepSeek 顯示賬戶餘額，OpenCode Zen Go 與 Command Code 顯示最緊迫的一個額度視窗； 未登記餘額介面的服務商改為彈文字說明 （不靜默）；按寵物獨立開關 碎碎念與對話 ：碎碎念按週期自動生成一句（說話動畫 + 氣泡，也可手動觸發）；對話在右鍵彈輸入框與寵物聊天，記憶持久化（瀏覽器 / 桌面共享同一份） 工作狀態聯動 ：監聽 DSH 會話事件，切「思考 / 工作 / 整理 / 等待 / 成功 / 出錯」檔位動畫 + 常駐氣泡；目標多輪任務只在真正收尾輪慶祝 系統通知 ：視窗失焦時彈系統 toast（對話完成 / 生成失敗 / 輸出截斷 / 許可權申請 / 使用者選擇） 桌面模式（可選） ：每隻寵物開一個獨立透明置頂局部小窗，與瀏覽器嚴格同行為、共用同一份素材與純邏輯（見下節） pet pack（額外寵物種類） ： pet/ 下建 種類名-config.json + 種類名-animation/ 即新增獨立動畫池與素材的全新種類，多例項共享素材（見「配置 → 方式四」） 自定義動畫 ：往 main-animation/webm/ 放 VP9-Alpha 的 .webm 即為新動畫，優先於包內素材 無障礙 ：支援 prefers-reduced-motion （減少動效時跳過 Q 彈擠壓與淡入切換） 🔌 對外介面（供其他外掛呼叫） 桌寵不只自己玩，也 對外開放兩條呼叫通道 ，讓別的外掛或指令碼能驅動它、讀它的狀態。 能做什麼 ：讓它說一句指定的話、播一段指定動畫、與它對話；讀它當前說的話、工作狀態、系統通知與餘額 為什麼開放 ：桌寵不該只是個擺設——比如一個「女僕」外掛巡檢驗完想說句話，就能讓桌寵當它的「實體」開口；也方便任何人基於它做二次開發 通道一 · HTTP ：掛在 DSH 自己的 Web 服務上（字首 /dsh-pet-7340 ，只監聽本機、無鑑權），跨程序、指令碼可直接調。動作類介面只回 {ok} ，資料統一從 GET /state 讀 通道二 · Cordis 服務 ：客戶端半側在 DSH web 頁面內註冊，同頁客戶端外掛用 ctx.get('petApi7340') 直接取，零網路、零埠；只在該頁面例項內有效，方法與返回見 CORDIS.md 相關檔案（HTTP 與 Cordis 各一套）： API.md —— HTTP 介面一覽（每個介面一句話，功能預覽） openapi.yaml —— 完整契約（OpenAPI 3.1，可直接匯入 Swagger UI / Postman） CORDIS.md —— 對外 Cordis 服務（客戶端半側，頁面內 ctx.get('petApi7340') ，不走網路） tools/api-tester.html —— HTTP 側示例：桌寵控制台，扮演第三方消費方，可直觀試用（ node tools/api-tester.cjs 啟動） tools/cordis-probe —— Cordis 側示例：扮演同頁客戶端外掛，用 ctx.get() 消費服務 相容性 作業系統 ：Windows / Linux / macOS 三端均可執行——瀏覽器 overlay 與桌面模式（Electron 透明置頂窗）行為完全一致；Electron 按平臺自動探測/下載（ electron.exe / Electron.app / linux 單檔案），無需手動安裝 無頭 / 無桌面環境 ：支援 Linux headless 等無圖形會話——桌面模式自動檢測顯示環境（Linux 無 DISPLAY / WAYLAND_DISPLAY 時判定無顯示、跳過桌面視窗，僅日誌告警），瀏覽器 overlay 不受影響 瀏覽器 ：瀏覽器 overlay 相容 Chromium 核心（Chrome / Edge 等）與 Firefox ——透明動畫依賴 VP9-Alpha webm，三者均已實測透明確認； 不支援 Safari （macOS 不認 webm alpha，透明渲染為黑底）——macOS 用 .mov 素材（GitHub Release assets-mov ），下載放入 + 改 ANIMATION_EXT 變數即可（見「②.5 Safari/HEVC 相容素材」） 多顯示器 ：支援多屏環境——跨屏漫遊/拋擲以各屏工作區為界，異構縮放（各屏 DPI 不同）、工作列條帶、螢幕之間空洞均正確判定（橫屏 / 豎屏 / 上下疊放皆可）；設定頁「鎖定在當前螢幕」可讓寵物（拋擲與漫遊）只在當前所在那塊屏內活動 🪟 桌面模式（可選，脫離瀏覽器） 外掛內建 雙模式 ：安裝後預設會拉起 獨立透明置頂小窗 ——為每隻桌面寵物各開一個局部視窗（跟隨寵物移動， 不鋪滿螢幕 ），與瀏覽器 overlay 嚴格同行為、功能完全對齊： 依賴 ：首次啟動自動探測/下載 Electron（ ~/.dsh/electron/ ，也可 cd dsh-pet && npm run ensure:electron 手動觸發）；缺失時僅日誌告警，不影響瀏覽器形態 開關 = 每隻寵物的必填欄位 display ： web = 僅瀏覽器 / desktop = 僅桌面 / both = 兩者 / none = 都不顯示；桌面模式渲染 display 含 desktop 的 全部 寵物（多開同屏，與瀏覽器一致），設定頁「桌寵配置」編輯即時生效 桌面端資料走獨立程序管道，不依賴 DSH 的 HTTP 路由，不受 web 訪問閘門影響 本地除錯： cd dsh-pet && npm run start:desktop -- http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-pet-7340/config （無宿主時自動回落 HTTP 路徑） 🧍 獨立執行（完全不開啟 DSH） 連 DSH 都不用開：外掛的宿主半邊跑在偽 ctx 上，由一個本機 HTTP 服務接管路由（ 路由表仍是外掛那一份 ）。 npm install -g dsh-pet # 必須 npm 裝；dsh plugin add 裝進 profile，bin 不在 PATH 上 dsh-pet-standalone # http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-pet-7340/（佔用則順延） dsh-pet-standalone --check # 只體檢 dsh-pet-standalone --port 3100

npm run build && npm run standalone # 倉庫裡（先構建） 能用 ：動畫鏈、點選/拖拽/甩拋、右鍵選單、多開、自定義動畫與表情包、pet pack。 不可用 ：餘額、碎碎念、對話、系統通知——返回帶 reason 的結構化失敗（見 API.md ）。 配置 ：與 DSH 同一份（ $DSH_HOME/dsh-pet/main-config.jsonc → 包內預設）。 只顯示 display 含 desktop / both 的例項 ；埠預設 3080； Ctrl+C 或 POST /shutdown 退出。 與 DSH 內執行可同時開 ，但共用 %APPDATA%\dsh-pet-electron-helper ，可能互相踩快取（僅告警）。 ⚙️ 餘額展示（Balance） 按 eventsRefreshSec.balance （秒）週期拉取當前服務商的餘額/用量資料，每次重新整理按檔位觸發一次餘額動畫，並在寵物頭頂彈出 聯想氣泡 （隨寵物大小等比縮放，10 秒自動消失）： DeepSeek 官方（ deepseek-official ） ：氣泡顯示賬戶餘額（如 餘額 ¥8.79 ）；餘額按 ¥20 滿額折算成已用百分比，分 6 檔播放動畫（錢袋滿溢 → 金袋叮噹 → 錢袋如常 → 數金皺眉 → 袋空如洗 → 分文不剩） OpenCode Zen Go（ opencode-go ） ：氣泡顯示 5h/周/月 三個額度視窗中最先告急的一個（如 周額度已用 88% / 2.5 天重置 ），同樣按已用百分比分檔 Command Code（ commandcode ，含 GOAT 等套餐） ：氣泡顯示 5h/周/月 三個額度視窗中最先告急的一個（與 opencode 同一口徑：剩餘額度最少者，通常先報 5h）；套餐無視窗限制時只報月度窗 暫不支援的服務商 ：未登記餘額介面的服務商 不播檔位動畫，改為彈一句文字說明 ——第一行「當前服務商暫不支援餘額查詢」，第二行報出當前 provider id（便於自查）；缺憑證 / 抓取失敗同理（原因寫在第二行）。自動輪詢只在 原因變化 時彈一次（不反覆打擾），手動 /balance 或桌面右鍵「檢視餘額」則每次都會彈 按寵物開關 ： pets[i].balanceEnabled （必填布林）控制該寵物是否觸發餘額動畫/顯示氣泡 所需憑據 ：對應 provider 的 API key（ deepseek-official → DEEPSEEK_API_KEY ； opencode-go → OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY ； commandcode → COMMANDCODE_API_KEY ），在 DSH 憑據中配置後啟用；未匹配的服務商不觸發動畫，改為彈上面的文字說明氣泡 ⚙️ 碎碎念與對話 碎碎念 ： pets[i].whisperEnabled 開啟後，按 eventsRefreshSec.whisper （秒，預設 300）週期自動生成一句——每隻寵物獨立週期、獨立文案；觸發時隨機抽 events.whisper 動畫 + 頭頂說話氣泡（10 秒消失）。預設開啟 手動觸發 ：右鍵選單「碎碎念」隨時來一句——不受 whisperEnabled 門控（該欄位只關自動週期輪詢） 對話 ：右鍵選單「對話」或 /chat 命令開啟輸入框，與寵物聊天——回覆走碎碎念同款展示（說話動畫 + 氣泡）；記憶持久化在 $DSH_HOME/dsh-pet/memory.json ，瀏覽器與桌面共享同一份；多寵物時先用 /pet 選擇對話目標 ⚙️ 工作狀態聯動（Work Status） pets[i].

title: ModernRelay/omnigraph
abstract:
Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology. Unified retrieval engine (vector/bm25/graph) · Git-style workflows · Open data format (Lance) Quickstart · Docs · Cookbooks · CLI llms.txt Omnigraph is engineered for the new workload introduced by long-horizon agents: Multiple agents sharing a typed world model to continuously retrieve and store context and coordinate work. Agents and UIs can become thin stateless consumers of a durable state. Capabilities Capability What it gives you Typed ontology Agents share one enforceable model of the domain. .pg schemas declare node and edge types, keys and constraints, and the engine enforces them on every write. Multimodal retrieval Agents assemble high-precision context in one query: graph traversal + vector ANN + full-text + Reciprocal Rank Fusion in one runtime, with filtering. Branching Agents propose reviewable changes instead of writing to main: a branch per agent or task, three-way merge, time travel across the whole graph. Declared as code A cluster.yaml declares graphs, schemas, stored queries, embedding providers and policies. cluster plan previews, cluster apply converges, Terraform-style. Security as code Cedar policy enforced server-side on every mutation , per graph or server-wide; bearer auth, server-resolved actors, audit tracking. Object-storage native, open format Scales at the lowest cost on local disk or any S3-compatible store: RustFS / MinIO, AWS S3 / R2 / GCS, Azure preview. Data lives in open, versioned Lance with native blob-as-data, and never leaves your store. What you can build Use case What it's for Company brain Org knowledge unified into one graph every agent can query Agentic memory Durable, versioned memory: a branch per agent or per task, merged on review Context graph Decision traces and codified tribal knowledge for retrieval Dev graph Issues & dependency model that coding agents read and write R&D / ML data layer Experiments and trials written into branches, versioned for training & eval Install curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/main/scripts/install.sh | bash This installs omnigraph (CLI) and omnigraph-server into ~/.local/bin from
published release binaries. Or with Homebrew: brew tap ModernRelay/tap
brew install ModernRelay/tap/omnigraph Set it up with an AI agent Omnigraph is built to be run by coding agents. Two ways in: Teach your agent the playbook. The omnigraph binary carries the omnigraph agent skill written for it: the operational
playbook covering cluster mode, the two config surfaces, schema evolution, query
linting, data writes, branches, Cedar policy, and the common gotchas. Export it
where your agent loads skills, so the skill always matches the installed CLI: omnigraph skill export ~ /.claude/skills/omnigraph --force With an older CLI that has no skill command, or none installed, npx skills add ModernRelay/omnigraph@omnigraph installs the copy on the
default branch instead. Or have an agent set it up from scratch. Paste this into Claude Code,
Codex, or any agent that can read a URL and run a shell command: Help me set up Omnigraph

1. Read the docs at https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph, starting with
   docs/user/clusters/index.md, then docs/user/deployment.md.
2. Skim the starter graphs and seed data in the cookbooks:
   https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks
3. Ask me what I want to build (company brain, agent memory, dev graph,
   research / R&D layer, …). Then stand up a cluster for it, load a little
   data, and run a query so I can see it working. For ready-to-run graphs with real seed data (company brain, VC operating system,
pharma & industry intel), ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks is the fastest way to see Omnigraph shaped to a real domain. Deploy A deployment is a cluster : a multigraph config directory that declares
its graphs, schemas, stored queries, and policies as code. You manage it Terraform-style : cluster plan previews the diff, cluster apply converges
it. omnigraph-server then boots from the cluster and brings every graph online
at /graphs/{id}/… , each behind its own policy. 1. Declare the cluster. company-brain/
├── cluster.yaml
├── people.pg          # schema for the "knowledge" graph
├── queries/           # stored queries: the .gq files ARE the declaration
│   └── people.gq
└── base.policy.yaml   # a Cedar policy bundle # cluster.yaml version : 1 metadata : name : company-brain storage : s3://company/clusters/company-brain # ledger, catalog, and graph data live here graphs : knowledge : schema : people.pg queries : queries/ # every `query <name>` in queries/*.gq registers policies : base : file : base.policy.yaml applies_to : [knowledge] # graph-bound; use [cluster] for server-level 2. Stand up your object store. On-prem, run RustFS (or MinIO); Omnigraph
writes Lance over the standard S3 API.
In the cloud, use S3 / R2 / GCS through AWS_* . Native az:// roots are also
available as a qualification preview. Every Azure writer, including cluster apply and the server, must use the checked-in admission wrapper;
follow the Azure deployment guide instead of running the bare commands below. 3. Converge and run. apply creates each graph, applies its schema, and
publishes queries and policies into the content-addressed catalog. It is
idempotent; re-running is always safe. omnigraph cluster validate # parse + typecheck everything omnigraph cluster plan --target ./company-brain # preview omnigraph cluster apply --target ./company-brain # converge # Boot the server from the cluster dir; storage resolves through cluster.yaml omnigraph-server --cluster company-brain --bind 0.0.0.0:8080 The bare commands above describe local and S3 deployments. See the cluster guide for the day-2 loop
(edit → plan → apply → restart), approval gates for destructive changes, drift
inspection, and recovery; the deployment guide for
containers, AWS/Railway/Azure, auth, and the object-store environment contracts. Query and mutate Define a server target with default_graph and set defaults.target once in ~/.omnigraph/config.yaml ( configuration ), and the
everyday commands stay short. Stored queries and mutations run by name : omnigraph query  search_docs --params ' {"q":"AI safety"} ' omnigraph mutate add_person  --params ' {"name":"Mina"} ' # Branch, review, merge across the whole graph; agents write in isolation omnigraph branch create --from main agent/ingest-42
omnigraph branch merge  agent/ingest-42 --into main An alias is shorter still: bind a target, graph, and stored query to one
name, then omnigraph alias triage runs it. For an ad-hoc target, any command
takes --target NAME|ADDRESS , plus --graph ID for a graph within a server
or direct root. Use --target ./graph.omni for a standalone graph. See the CLI reference . Security & governance Engine-wide enforcement: every write path goes through the same Cedar gate, so the HTTP server, the CLI, and the embedded SDK obey identical rules. Declared in the cluster: a policy bundle is bound to graphs (or the whole server) via policies: → applies_to . Scoped: rules apply per graph, per branch, or server-wide. No plaintext tokens: bearer tokens are hashed at startup and compared in constant time. Forge-proof identity: the actor is resolved server-side from the token; clients can't set it. See the policy guide . Clients & SDKs Client Use it for Where TypeScript SDK typed access from Node / TS @modernrelay/omnigraph · source MCP server bridge Omnigraph to LLM hosts (Claude, Codex, …) @modernrelay/omnigraph-mcp HTTP / OpenAPI any language, the wire contract the server's OpenAPI spec Python SDK typed access from Python coming soon Both npm packages are versioned in lockstep with omnigraph-server .

title: macro-inc/macro
abstract: Sign up · Docs · Book demo · Website · Feature requests · Contribute · Hiring Macro is the all-in-one workspace for you and your team. It unifies email + messages + docs + tasks + agents + CRM into a single fast interface with shared team-level memory. Everything in your workspace is @linked and searchable so your team (and your agents) never have to switch tools. Why Macro We built Macro because we wanted a single operating system for our startup. There are many good software products, and we used them all — Slack, Linear, Notion, HubSpot, and Superhuman — but they don't work together as one system. As we scaled our last venture to ~20 people things started to break: every team got their own tools and the company was held together by MCP and Zapier. The company was not computable. It was chaotic. Macro is a complete redesign of work software from the ground up as a single system. Designed by us in NYC and Toronto, dogfooded by our team of ~15 for two years. Built in SolidJS and Rust for speed and reliability. We're focused on building something that any small company or team at a larger company can use as their "operating system". Features Macro is composed of 'blocks' designed to be modular, extensible, and work together like Lego. For each block, we studied the best prior art and tried to make it even better. Each surface is purpose-built for its job rather than composed from a generic block primitive — but every one of them shares the same backend; cross-references between a doc and a task, or a channel message and an email, are natively stored as a bidirectional graph . Block Docs What it does Email Docs → Multi-account unified inbox, keyboard shortcuts, and shared inboxes. Gmail. Messages Docs → Channels and direct messages designed for focused technical discussions. Tasks Docs → Linear-inspired tasks, tightly integrated with channels, email, and agents. Docs Docs → Real-time collaborative, markdown-native docs built on CRDTs, with @mentions. Canvas Docs → 2D board with embedded @links to tasks, files, and emails. Agents Docs → Unified, team-level memory. Can take action on your behalf. Calls Docs → Recorded, transcribed, and logged to team memory for agents. File storage Docs → Auto-imported from email and channels, fully searchable. Pull requests Docs → Linked to tasks, embeddable in channels, available to agents. CRM Docs → Customer and contact objects, custom properties, email sync, enrichment. Multiple email inboxes w/ good AI tools, integrated CRM Macro Mail is inspired by Superhuman's keyboard-first interface with a few key additions: Multi-account. Triage all your Google accounts in a single inbox, with the same tagging and sharing system. Or triage individually. Unified inbox: emails, messages, @mentions, and tasks to complete, all in the same list. Use j k and e to navigate everything. Better AI, with a tools/MCP surface designed to work across inboxes and to help your agents more accurately retrieve information. For example, we expose a unified search tool that allows agents to search all file attachment PDFs (parsed out of email) directly, rather than pulling email threads then attachments. You can also draft, edit and send emails right from AI chats, without opening your email. Multitasking ability — Macro has a built-in window manager that lets you create 3+ splits (scales with monitor size) so you can draft emails while reviewing prior threads. Company/Contact objects. Macro has native CRM capability so you can cmd+k to a contact, like tim@acme.com to see all emails between you and that person, or companies, to see all emails and files between everyone on your team and everyone at that company, e.g. @acme.com . All of this right from your email without having to open a heavyweight CRM like HubSpot or Salesforce. Email aggregation by contact or company is also available to your agents so they can better assist with CRM-type queries and actions. Macro Mail lives in the same interface as channels, docs, tasks, and code. From any email, hit "task" to create a linked task, e.g. a ticket for an engineer from a customer support email. @mention emails in documents, e.g. @Re: Contract Signature.eml inside of Todos.md. In Macro, your email is brought into the fold with all of your tools, and your team, in the same permissions system: just hit Share to share an email to any DM or channel — no need to screenshot. Email docs → Team chat for focused technical discussions Macro Chat is designed to be more focused than Slack. The first couple of replies show inline and the rest collapse into a thread, so a busy channel stays readable. Threads are permissioned severally so you can share threads across channels by copying links. Everything is stored in a bidirectional graph, so tasks @link to messages that created them, customer support emails tie into support channels, CRM records get updated when they're discussed in messages, etc. The core idea is that (i) messaging should be the centerpiece around which tasks, mail, docs, and content management are built, all in a lightweight way, and agents should be first-class citizens like human users and (ii) messaging needs to be more focused and readable for technical conversations, and not turn into battles where context is lost and progress is indistinguishable from noise. Messages docs → Task management built around chat Linear recently published a report that issue tracking is dead. We agree with that, but the stronger form is that issue tracking never really worked, at least for us. We really tried and we blamed ourselves, but as we talked to other companies, it turns out that nobody was using their issue tracker "correctly". And if that's the case, the problem is the design of the tool, not the companies that use it. The core problem with traditional issue trackers or project management tools is that they get out of date. The reason they get out of date is that (i) they're a separate system from where the conversation really happens in team chat (e.g. Slack, Macro, Discord, etc.) and (ii) they don't add much benefit beyond tracking the work. They're a chore with near-term costs and only the promise of long-term benefit. They're too rigid compared to a 2D canvas, too opinionated, and don't match how your project actually functions. The solution isn't to forgo tracking entirely. We tried that and it was a different form of chaos. The solution we've found is lightweight issues tightly coupled to your channels and DMs, so that issue tracking naturally occurs where the conversation itself happens. Creating tasks in Macro is easy. Where possible, tasks created are bidirectionally linked to the creating context (e.g. a customer email) so the full chain is auditable from "why are we doing this" → task → agent → pull request, all in one system. Create a task from an email From anywhere via c t From a markdown doc with /task From any - [ ] bullet by highlighting and clicking "Task" @Macro create tasks in any channel or DM In any agent chat Via external MCP, API or SDK Tasks docs → @linked markdown docs powered by CRDTs We wanted everything in a single markdown editor without switching tools. Native markdown compatibility and bulk/import export (see "file over app" paradigm) Live collaboration with CRDTs and Cloudflare durable objects make it feel like you're editing on the same computer. Edits come in ~instantly instead of ka-chunking like Google Docs Version control: history and forking, with a neat UI for scrubbing history. This is still in v1, there's a lot to do to get it closer to git, or we may eventually add git compatibility. Offline editing and reconciliation. @-linked to everything in your workspace: email, docs, tasks, messages, channels, companies, contacts, etc. Like Notion but multi-modal Mobile-friendly, in our iOS app or on the web (Android app coming soon) Agent native editing, powered by swarms of agents operating as peers in the CRDT collaboration system like human collaborators.

title: Jamailar/Beav
abstract: Beav AI 自媒體工作臺 從資訊與選題，到圖文創作、口播剪輯和持續運營的一站式 AI 工作空間。 本地優先 · 賬號長期記憶 · AI 圖片與影片剪輯 · macOS / Windows / Linux 官網高速下載 影片教程 RedBox 已更名為 Beav ；原有本地資料和工作空間不受影響。 做自媒體，時間都去哪了？ 你每天遇到的麻煩 Beav 的做法 手機上刷到好內容只能收藏，回到電腦就找不到了 在手機上貼上分享連結，一鍵存進 電腦知識庫 ，影片自動下載轉寫，還能 自動拆解 成選題、結構、鏡頭和逐字文案 對標賬號一天看一遍，看完就忘 訂閱博主 ，新內容每天自動同步入庫，還能選擇自動拆解 每天早上不知道寫什麼 每天 09:00 生成 運營日報 和今日計劃， 熱點 頁按你的賬號方向給各平臺熱榜打分 通用 AI 寫出來的東西沒有“你”的味道 每個賬號一個 空間 ，定位、受眾、文風、偏好和已發內容都進長期記憶，AI 每次接著上次的積累寫 寫完稿還要去別的軟體做封面、剪影片、配字幕 同一個對話裡寫稿、用 圖片模板 生圖、在 剪輯器 裡智慧剪口播、加字幕和動畫、AI 配音 釋出前在電腦和手機之間來回傳圖、複製文案 稿件自動打包成各平臺 素材包 ，排進 內容日曆 ，手機掃碼直接領取圖片和文案 已經在用 Codex、Claude Code，不想再換一個 AI 一鍵 接入 Agent ，讓你常用的 AI 直接讀寫 Beav 的素材庫、知識庫和稿件 Beav 不是又一個聊天框，而是一個為內容創作者準備的、會越用越懂你的 素材庫 + 運營工作臺 。 一條完整的內容線 手機刷到，電腦做完，手機發出去 靈感大多是在手機上刷到的，創作卻要在電腦上完成，最後又得回到手機發布。Beav 把這條路打通了：手機和電腦連同一個 Wi-Fi，掃一下二維碼就能互傳，不用裝手機 App。 手機刷到，一鍵存到電腦 ：在電腦知識庫點「手機上傳」，手機掃碼開啟「儲存到知識庫」頁面。之後在小紅書、抖音、B 站、YouTube、微博、知乎、公眾號等 App 裡複製分享連結，貼上進來就行，連分享文案一起粘也沒關係，一次最多 50 條。手機相簿裡的照片、影片和錄音也能直接傳進素材庫。配對一次，90 天內收藏頁面地址就能直接開啟。 存進來就自動拆解 ：提交前勾選「儲存後拆解」，電腦會自動下載、轉寫，並把每條內容拆成選題、結構、鏡頭節奏、拍攝指令碼和帶時間的原文案，拆出來的片段直接進素材庫。訂閱的博主也能開啟「自動拆解新內容」，對方一更新就自動入庫、自動拆好。 在電腦上用 AI 創作 ：拿剛存的內容找選題、寫稿、做封面、剪影片，最後打包成各平臺的素材包。 掃碼到手機發布 ：在素材包、稿件或知識庫卡片上點手機圖示，手機掃碼開啟領取頁，原圖儲存到相簿，標題和正文一鍵複製，直接去 App 釋出。圖片、影片、文件和整個資料夾也都能這樣分享到手機。 手機刷到：掃碼配對，貼上連結存到電腦並自動拆解 電腦做完：掃碼到手機，儲存原圖、複製文案去釋出 開啟主頁，就知道今天做什麼 主頁把一天的工作放在一屏裡： 會話看板 ：AI 在後臺幹活，你只看三欄。「等你處理」是 AI 停下來問你的問題，「待檢視」是做完等你驗收的結果，「進行中」是還在跑的任務。點開卡片，會話在右側抽屜裡繼續聊，不用離開主頁。 內容排期 ：本週要發什麼、哪篇還是初稿、哪篇過了計劃日還沒發，一眼看清；可在月 / 周 / 年檢視之間切換，拖動即可改期，節日和節氣會標在日曆上方便借勢。 小工具 ：常用的小工具和你讓 AI 做出來的專屬小工具，都在頂部一鍵開啟。 月檢視：排期、狀態與當天產出 點開會話，在右側抽屜裡直接驗收和繼續聊 找選題：日報、熱點和你的賬號對得上 運營日報 ：每天 09:00 結合你的賬號方向，整理今日計劃和值得跟進的發現，每條都帶來源連結，點「去創作」就開一個新對話。 熱點 ：「適合我的賬號」按匹配度給全網熱點打分，並標出它在各平臺榜單上的位置；右側並排展示小紅書、抖音、B 站、微博、知乎、百度、頭條等熱榜。看到合適的，直接發起 AI 討論或存進選題池。 寫稿：懂你賬號的 AI 寫手 在新對話裡說出目標即可，例如「用知識庫裡的秋季新品調研，寫一篇小紅書筆記」。AI 會讀取你存過的資料和賬號檔案，按平臺寫出完整作品：標題、正文、話題標籤，必要時連配圖一起生成，最後交付一個可以直接釋出的 素材包 ，在對話右側就能預覽、標記已釋出或去釋出。 步驟可見 ：每一步做了什麼、呼叫了哪些工具，都在對話裡摺疊展示，長任務可以隨時停下或繼續。 會問你，不會亂猜 ：遇到需要你拍板的地方，AI 會在輸入框上方彈出問題卡片，點選項或數字鍵就能回答，「跳過」則交給 AI 按推薦方案決定。 稿件即文件 ：稿件按資料夾管理，開啟就是 Obsidian 式即時預覽編輯器，邊改邊自動儲存，右側 AI 側欄隨時幫你改開頭、換標題。 越寫越像你 ：可以讓 AI 讀一批你過去的稿件或知識庫內容學習文風，長期偏好會在之後的任務裡自動沿用。 稿件：即時預覽編輯 + AI 側欄 需要你決定時，AI 用問題卡片來問 做圖和剪影片：不用再切換軟體 圖片與封面 ：新對話下方就是模板庫，按行業和用途（封面、圖片、小紅書、影片）篩選，點「使用模板」填文字、換參考圖即可生成；看到喜歡的圖片，也能讓 AI 拆解成你自己的模板反覆使用。 智慧剪口播 ：把錄好的口播影片交給 AI，說一句剪輯目標就行。AI 逐字轉寫、結合語義和停頓，找出口頭語、重說和多餘的句子，列成一張可核對的剪輯方案；確認後自動應用到時間線，再補上字幕、重點花字、畫中畫和講解動畫。 完整剪輯器 ：多軌時間線、字幕軌、花字與特效軌、畫中畫、關鍵幀、轉場、調色、音訊和人聲降噪都在裡面；AI 助手可以結合當前工程繼續改，所有操作都能撤銷。匯出可選目錄、看進度，也能單獨匯出 SRT / WebVTT 字幕。 智慧剪口播：哪裡刪、為什麼刪，一目瞭然 剪輯器：字幕、花字、畫中畫和配樂都在時間線上 此外還有 AI 配音與多語言配音、靜態圖轉影片、影片模板等能力，都從對話裡直接呼叫。 積累素材：知識庫和素材庫 知識庫 ：儲存小紅書、抖音、B 站、YouTube、X、微博、知乎、公眾號等連結，也能關聯本地資料夾、Obsidian 和 Eagle。影片會自動下載和轉寫，評論區也能一起存。 拆解爆款 ：儲存時勾選「儲存後拆解」，或對已有條目點「拆解」，就能拿到選題、結構、鏡頭節奏、拍攝指令碼和帶時間的原文案，拆出來的片段直接進素材庫。 訂閱博主 ：訂閱對標賬號後每天自動同步新內容，可開啟「自動拆解新內容」，每日額度可調。 素材庫 ：像訪達一樣管理圖片、影片、文案、配樂、提示詞和選題；支援資料夾、多選拖放、右鍵選單、空格預覽、手機掃碼上傳。入庫的素材會被 AI 理解（轉寫、拆解、視覺索引），之後用一句話就能找出來。 拆解：一條爆款的選題、結構和鏡頭 素材庫：圖片、影片、文案、配樂、提示詞、選題 讓你自己的 AI 也能用：接入 Agent 已經習慣用 Codex、Claude Code、WorkBuddy、Claude 桌面版或 Cursor？開啟「接入 Agent」，選中工具點「連線」，Beav 會直接寫好它的 MCP 配置，不用裝外掛、不用敲命令。連好後，在這些工具裡新開一個對話，就能： 搜尋、讀取和存入 Beav 的素材庫、知識庫、賬號檔案和稿件； 把創作任務派給 Beav 的 Agent，或讓它們把成品寫回 Beav； 共享同一份賬號記憶和創作偏好。 只想把 Beav 當成「帶 AI 理解的素材庫」用？在頭像選單切換到 素材庫模式 （⌘⇧M），介面收起對話和創作入口，只保留素材庫、熱點和日曆，交給你常用的 Agent 去排程。Beav 也會在本機提供一個素材庫網頁，可以直接在 Codex 等工具的側欄裡開啟。 接入 Agent：選工具，點連線 本機素材庫網頁：在外部 AI 工具側欄裡也能完整使用 小工具與技能市場 小工具 ：影片文案批次提取、連結素材下載、字幕轉寫、AI 配音、去 AI 後設資料、圖片轉 Live 圖、賬號運營規劃……也可以直接讓 AI 幫你做一個專屬小工具，做好後出現在主頁。 技能市場 ：按調研與選題、熱點追蹤、文案風格、指令碼最佳化、圖片製作、影片製作分類，一鍵安裝，讓 AI 更貼近具體的運營任務。 適合這些場景 一個人運營一個賬號 為賬號建一個空間，匯入自己的主頁讓 AI 初始化定位和記憶。平時在手機上刷到好內容就順手存進電腦知識庫並自動拆解；每天看日報和熱點挑選題，在對話裡寫稿、出圖，排進日曆，釋出前手機掃碼領取。Beav 會記住你的定位、文風和已經發過的內容，避免選題撞車。 口播 / 知識類影片創作者 先在知識庫裡拆解幾條同領域的爆款，學習它們的開頭和節奏；寫好口播稿後錄製，把原片交給 AI 智慧剪口播，刪掉口頭語和重說，再補字幕、花字、畫中畫和講解動畫，匯出成片。 小紅書圖文 / 公眾號作者 訂閱對標博主每天同步，評論區高頻問題沉澱成選題；用模板一次做出封面和整組配圖，稿件自動打包成小紅書或公眾號素材包，公眾號還可以傳送到草稿箱。 多賬號、代運營和小團隊 每個賬號或品牌一個空間，素材、記憶和稿件互不串味；用 ⌥⌘1–9 快速切換。週期任務（如每週資料週報、每天的選題雷達）交給日曆定時跑，結果在會話看板裡統一驗收。 已經在用 Codex / Claude Code 的人 切到素材庫模式，把 Beav 當成會自動整理、轉寫和拆解的素材庫；通過「接入 Agent」讓你熟悉的 AI 直接取用素材、寫稿並把成品放回 Beav。 部署在伺服器上用 Linux 伺服器版可以通過瀏覽器訪問，適合放在一臺常開的機器上跑訂閱同步和定時任務。 快速開始 前往 下載頁 安裝 Beav（macOS / Windows / Linux）。 登入後為你的賬號或品牌 建立一個空間 ，貼上自己的主頁連結，讓 AI 在對話中初始化賬號檔案、定位和記憶。 在 設定 → AI 使用官方 AI，或配置自己的模型供應商（OpenAI-compatible 介面、本地模型等）。 往知識庫裡存幾條對標內容，或訂閱幾個對標博主；需要網頁一鍵採集時，從 最新 Release 獲取 Chrome / Edge 擴展。 回到主頁，從日報、熱點或選題池挑一個方向，在新對話裡說出你的目標，剩下的交給 Beav。 不確定某個功能在哪裡？直接在對話裡問 Beav，它會查內建的使用手冊，告訴你當前版本的入口。 部分新功能會隨新版本陸續提供，安裝包與本頁描述的進度可能不同，請以所安裝版本的實際入口為準。完整版本變化見 更新日誌 。 功能一覽 採集與知識 選題與運營 寫作與協作 圖片與小工具 影片剪輯 手機貼上連結 / 外掛 / 連結儲存 每日運營日報與今日計劃 按平臺寫圖文、口播稿、長文 圖片 / 封面 / 影片模板 智慧剪口播：口頭語與重說 影片自動下載與轉寫 「適合我的賬號」熱點打分 賬號檔案與長期記憶 從圖片建立自己的模板 字幕編輯與 SRT / WebVTT 匯出 爆款拆解：選題、結構、鏡頭、文案 多平臺熱榜並排瀏覽 稿件即時預覽編輯、自動儲存 去 AI 後設資料、圖片轉 Live 圖 花字、畫中畫與講解動畫 博主訂閱、每日同步與自動拆解 選題池與靈感記錄 各平臺素材包與版本管理 title: harry0703/MangoDisk
abstract: MangoDisk Disk cleanup, storage analysis, and privacy protection for macOS , Windows , and Linux English · 簡體中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Русский What MangoDisk Can Do Storage 1. Deep Cleanup Find cleanable content scattered across the system, applications, developer tools, and local projects in one scan. MangoDisk saves you from checking each location manually and groups the results by reclaimable space: System and user caches : Reclaim space taken up over time by system temporary files, diagnostic data, and rebuildable caches. Application caches : Keep application caches, logs, update packages, and temporary content from quietly consuming more and more storage. Browser data : Reclaim space used by cached and temporary web data from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave, Arc, Opera, and other browsers. Developer tools and Xcode : Quickly recover substantial storage used by package managers, IDEs, compiler caches, and Xcode development data. Container caches : Free up space used by inactive build caches and rebuildable data from Docker and other container tools. Project build artifacts : Recover space used by rebuildable dependencies, caches, and build directories across Node.js, Rust, Gradle, Swift, Python, .NET, Godot, CMake, and other projects. AI models and caches : Quickly spot large local AI models, download caches, and temporary transfer files. Application optimization : Shrink supported applications without affecting normal use, leaving more room on your disk. Smart recommendations help you make safe choices quickly. You can also review items individually and see the estimated reclaimable space upfront, keeping every cleanup predictable and under your control. 2. Large File Cleanup Quickly find the largest files and reclaim space used by old installers, videos, archives, and other bulky content without digging through folders one by one. 3. Duplicate File Cleanup Reclaim space taken up by duplicate copies without treating files as duplicates just because they share a name. Smart selection keeps at least one file in every group, so cleanup stays effortless and safe. 4. Disk Space Analysis See where your disk space is going at a glance. Switch between a treemap and a sunburst chart , and choose how many levels to display to explore space usage and folder structure. Browse folders alongside the file list to quickly find the largest folders and files and decide what to clean up. Privacy & Security 5. Privacy Cleanup Keep browsing history, searches, cookies, recent items, and clipboard data from lingering on your computer. Clear traces left by browsers, applications, and the system to reduce exposure of your activity and make everyday privacy easier to manage. System Tools 6. Application Uninstall and Cleanup Uninstall applications and clear related caches, settings, and leftovers so removing an application actually gives you the space back. Potential personal files are handled cautiously to reduce the risk of accidental deletion. 7. Startup Item Management Reduce unnecessary startup delays and background resource use, so your computer starts faster and feels lighter. Turn items back on at any time when you need them again. 8. System Optimization Reduce unnecessary settings that slow down your system or get in the way. Balance performance, privacy, and personal preferences so your computer feels faster and easier to use. 9. System Maintenance Fix common problems like missing search results, incorrect icons, no sound, or network connection failures—without hunting down fixes or typing complex commands. Get your computer back to normal sooner. Activity 10. Operation History Keep a clear record of every cleanup and system change. See how much space you recovered, what completed successfully, and whether anything still needs your attention. Resource Usage and Memory Management Available since version 1.1.1 Check CPU and memory usage, network speeds, and disk activity at a glance. See which apps use the most memory and free up memory with a click when resources are running low. Keep these details in your menu bar, taskbar, or system tray—no need to open the main window. AI Explanations Available since version 1.1.0 Unsure what an item does or what might happen if you change it? AI explanations use the item's description and current scan results to explain its purpose and what to consider before taking action. Spend less time looking things up and make more informed choices. Get explanations directly from items in Deep Cleanup (built-in rules), Privacy Cleanup, Startup Item Management, System Optimization, and System Maintenance. Official releases include free explanations each day, with the option to connect your own AI service. AI offers guidance; you decide which actions to take. Safety and Rules Important MangoDisk puts data safety ahead of reclaiming more space. Cleanup rules and system optimizations only ship after their safety boundaries are clearly defined and they pass validation on real systems. MangoDisk scans in read-only mode by default. Before cleanup, deletion, uninstall, or system setting changes begin, you can review and confirm exactly what will happen. Results are saved to Operation History. System Optimization only uses built-in, validated settings. It never accepts arbitrary registry paths, terminal commands, or scripts. MangoDisk reads each setting again after changing it and calls out high-impact items and changes that require administrator access or a restart. MangoDisk maintains its own cleanup rules. Third-party projects may provide research leads, but a candidate rule is only accepted after reliable sources, safe boundaries, and real-system behavior have been verified. Anything without a clear safety boundary is excluded. The complete rule library and revision history are open for inspection: view the MangoDisk cleanup rule library . Screenshots Deep Cleanup Find cleanable content across the system, applications, developer tools, and projects to reclaim more space Large File Cleanup Find the files taking up the most space without digging through folders Duplicate File Cleanup Safely remove exact duplicates while keeping at least one copy Disk Space Analysis See where your storage is going and quickly find the largest files and folders Startup Item Management Reduce unnecessary startup programs for faster sign-in and less background activity Application Uninstall and Cleanup Uninstall applications and remove related leftovers to reclaim more space System Optimization Optimize performance, privacy, and everyday usability in one click System Maintenance Fix common system issues quickly and get your computer back to normal Privacy Cleanup Leave fewer activity traces behind and keep everyday use more private Before You Begin Caution Cleanup, permanent deletion, and uninstall operations may not be reversible. Review the selected content and keep reliable backups of important data. Before running system maintenance or changing a startup item or system setting, make sure you understand its purpose and impact. Some system optimizations can affect security, privacy, battery life, or update behavior. Desktop App Download MangoDisk from the official download page or GitHub Releases , then follow the instructions for your operating system below. macOS Requirements: macOS Monterey 12.5 or later. Install with Homebrew: brew install --cask harry0703/tap/mangodisk Manual installation: Download the DMG from the official download page , open it, and drag MangoDisk into the Applications folder. Windows Requirements: 64-bit Windows 10 or later. Install with PowerShell: irm https: // get.mangodisk.app | iex Install with WinGet (official source): winget install -- id MangoDisk.MangoDisk -- exact -- source winget Manual installation: Download the Windows installer from the official download page and follow the installation prompts. Linux Recommended: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or later, on x64 or ARM64. Available as .deb packages and AppImages.

Watch it appear on the infinite canvas in real-time with streaming animation. Modify existing designs by selecting elements and chatting. 🤖 Concurrent Agent Teams The orchestrator decomposes complex pages into spatial sub-tasks. Multiple AI agents work on different sections simultaneously — hero, features, footer — all streaming in parallel with per-member canvas indicators. 🧠 Multi-Model Intelligence Automatically adapts to each model's capabilities.
